nodes.label: laptop memory - the 2026-07-23 combine sweep and hybrid results

Frozen copy taken 2026-08-03 of the laptop's live memory file - evidence of what this machine believed at that date, listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md section 7. All gold-100, retrieval-only, id-metrics computed locally, metric recall_id (union) plus nDCG@50 from meta.chunk_ids, with a conjunctive decision rule of permutation-Holm AND BCa-CI AND sign AND Cliff. The combine rebuild payoff: the un-normalized-sum combine was replaced by per-path normalization plus strength-graded modifiers and a weighted sum over the union, taking det default 0.7039 to 0.7339, +0.030. The haiku combine sweep with cross-part live, 3-8 parts per question: baseline haiku default 0.6039 recall / 0.416 nDCG; global-norm 0.6812 (+0.077) better on both; none/raw 0.6536 (+0.050) better on both; absolute 0.5359 (-0.068) worse; max with corroboration off n.s. on recall but nDCG -0.026, so corroboration by summation helps ORDERING; facets at STR_FACET=1.0 n.s. on both. The verdict is that the principled per-path and absolute normalization LOSES and the winner lets stated scope dominate. The new hybrid arm (v3/pipelines/hybrid.py) is min-max late fusion of lucene and vector with HERB_HYBRID_ALPHA; at a matched ~500-id budget artefact haiku-global reads 0.6812 and artefact det 0.7339 against pure vector 0.4100, hybrid a=0.5 0.3883 and pure lucene 0.2742. Cluster-K on the fixed machinery: clusterK 0.7341 / nDCG 0.4748 and clusterK + global-norm 0.7492 / 0.4756 - but K=50 on all 100 questions, so the curve-decides-K mechanism is INERT and the gain is the progressive-frontier ORDERING, not the K-selection
